purpose: A coherent loop through Tasmania's east coast, central highlands and southwest wilderness edge, built around scenic viewpoints, half-day hikes and wildlife, with quiet-hour timing at the icons.
routeRationale: Hobart in, Hobart out with a clockwise loop: Tasman Peninsula, east coast up to Freycinet, inland to Cradle Mountain, down through the Derwent Valley back to Hobart. Each base sits within the 150-minute daily ceiling of its day's stops; onl
assumptions: No gravel roads used for driving legs
One special meal reserved for Hobart or Freycinet
Quiet-hour timing prioritised at Cradle Mountain and Freycinet
tradeoffs: Skips the far west coast (Strahan, Queenstown) to keep driving within the daily ceiling
Skips Bruny Island to avoid an extra ferry detour and base change
One long relocation day (Freycinet to Cradle Mountain) trades stops for distance
Prioritises Cradle Mountain over Southwest National Park, which is unreachable by road

unresolved: Track conditions and any fire trail closures at Cradle Mountain and Freycinet must be verified nearer the date
Shuttle bus operating hours at Cradle Mountain must be checked
Port Arthur opening hours and any timed-entry requirements must be verified
bookingPriorities: Cradle Mountain lodge (limited availability in spring)
Special dinner reservation in Hobart on the last night

foodStrategy: Breakfast kept light and near base each morning
Packed lunches on all outdoor hiking days
One special dinner reserved for the final night in Hobart
Local specialities (oysters, seafood) taken near the route, not as detours

transport.summary: Self-drive loop in a rental car, staying within a 150-minute daily driving ceiling except on the two relocation days.
notes: No gravel roads used; all routes are sealed
Cradle Mountain requires the park shuttle bus rather than private car during peak hours
Mountain passes on the highlands crossing are manageable in a standard car

beforeYouGo: Verify Cradle Mountain shuttle bus schedule and any parking permit requirements
Check Port Arthur Historic Site opening hours and ticketing
Confirm weather forecast for Wineglass Bay and Dove Lake hikes, both weather-sensitive
packing: Layered clothing for alpine weather at Cradle Mountain

backups.trigger: Rain or high wind at Cradle Mountain
backups.alternative: Shift to Enchanted Walk and visitor centre exhibits, defer Dove Lake to the following morning if schedule allows

backups.trigger: Cape Raoul track closed or too strenuous
backups.alternative: Substitute the shorter Waterfall Bay to Tatnells Hill walk on the same peninsula
